clue.text: Helping to collect money to marry

indicators.note: to collect means the helping gathers the money inside itself

parts.note: a helping of cake is a slice
P, for penny, is a small unit of money

explanation.surface: Someone helps with fundraising for a mass wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'marry', which the OCR read as 'many'. 'to collect' puts P inside SLICE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be spliced is slang for being wed, from joining two ropes together.

clue.text: A number getting work climbing in India

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone takes a job that involves going up in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns A + NO + OP upwards in this down clue, giving the letters in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: The old spelling names a city in Maharashtra, now usually Pune.

clue.text: Eminent tenor keeping to beat

annotationWithheld.why: Eminent tenor keeping to beat: tenor gives IMPORT, but no reading of 'keeping to beat' supplies the closing ANT

clue.text: Catch up accomplice right away

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the remaining letters are read bottom to top
right away means the letter for right is taken out

parts.note: a partner in crime is an accomplice

explanation.surface: Police nab a criminal's sidekick immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes R from PARTNER, leaving PARTNE; 'up' then reverses that to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare someone is to catch them by a trick.

clue.text: Strong players lead a club

indicators.note: lead means the players come in front of the club

parts.note: the players in a play are its cast
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A team's stars head up a sports club.
explanation.walkthrough: IRON is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbreakable and firm is described as made of cast metal, so it is figuratively robust.

clue.text: Relations on the way split a tyre — a clean burst

indicators.note: split means the following letters are broken apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cyclist's tyre bursts cleanly on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' is the anagram signal; the first 'a' is a link. 'Relations' means stories: Chaucer's pilgrims tell them on their journey to the cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's work is a collection of stories told by pilgrims while travelling, relations being narratives.

clue.text: Nearest to upright of two ways to hold raised sword

indicators.note: to hold means the two roads wrap round the sword

parts.note: ST, for street, is one way
ST, for street, is the second way

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the sword is read upwards

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: Two roads are positioned to keep a sword held aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the sword upward in this down clue, and 'to hold' makes the two streets wrap round it. 'Nearest to upright' means most nearly vertical.
explanation.definitionFit: The most precipitous slope is the one closest to vertical.

clue.text: Victor losing head in target area

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word for victor is dropped

parts.note: a victor is a winner

explanation.surface: A champion loses his head in a shooting zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' removes W from WINNER. Victor is also the radio code word for V, a likely false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: On an archery or shooting board, the ring next to the bull is the inner.

clue.text: Command without one of the big gums

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the guns surround the one

parts.note: ordnance is heavy artillery
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An order to fire without one of the large cannons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, so ORDNANCE goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree or regulation issued by authority is an order.

clue.text: Qualification to challenge a Name in the city

annotationWithheld.why: Qualification to challenge a Name in the City: COMPETE + N leaves CE, which 'the City' (EC) does not give without a reversal indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: Qualification to challenge a Name in the city

clue.text: Shifting dune revealing naturist, perhaps

indicators.note: shifting suggests sand dunes moving, so the letters rearrange

explanation.surface: Moving sands expose someone enjoying the beach unclothed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shifting' rearranges DUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist is an example of someone unclothed; 'perhaps' marks it as one instance.

clue.text: Bearing the cost of delivery?

definitions.meaning: one's bearing is one's posture or deportment

explanation.definitionFit: Deportment is how someone holds themselves, and the fee for transporting goods is also called this.

clue.text: Mother or father before rift

annotationWithheld.why: Mother or father before rift: the definition is 'Mother or father' but PA must come from 'father' too, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: A herd returning to protective enclosure

indicators.note: returning means the letters of the pieces go back the other way

parts.note: a mob is a herd or crowd

explanation.surface: A herd of animals heads back to its stockade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns A + MOB round. A boma is an East African stockade for livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: In East Africa a boma is a thorn fence or stockade sheltering livestock.

clue.text: Take time in choice of theatrical performance

indicators.note: in means the time is placed inside the choice

parts.note: an option is a choice
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone takes their time choosing a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'Theatrical' points to the operating theatre in a hospital, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery takes place in an operating theatre, so a surgical procedure is a performance there.

clue.text: Inferior accommodation for headquarters soldiers before start of training

indicators.note: before means the soldiers come ahead of the letter from training

parts.note: a base is a headquarters
men is a common crossword word for soldiers

indicators.note: start of means only the first letter of training is used

explanation.surface: Poor quarters for soldiers at HQ before training begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' gives T from training.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar flat is lower, below ground level, so inferior in the sense of beneath.

clue.text: Postponements upset plan about speaker's appearance

indicators.note: about means the turned plan goes round the speaker
upset in a down clue means the plan is turned upside down

parts.note: an aim is a plan
an orator is a speaker

explanation.surface: Delays disrupt a plan for a speaker to appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the plan upside down in this down clue (MIA), and 'about' wraps that round the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A moratorium is a suspension or delay, so its plural means deferrals.

clue.text: Vehicle made from cannibalized phaetons

indicators.note: cannibalized means the parts are taken apart and reused in a new order

explanation.surface: A carriage built from parts of old open carriages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cannibalized' rearranges PHAETONS. A phaeton is a light open carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a light open horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: One willing to provide treats to order

indicators.note: to order means the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone happy to supply sweets on demand.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'willing'. 'order' rearranges TREATS TO. The definition puns on making a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who makes a will.

clue.text: Run to shelter on way back from wind

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: on way back means the pieces are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side

explanation.surface: A walker runs for cover on the return trip from a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on way back' turns LEE + R round.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel in a line is to wind it on a spool.

clue.text: Be about to go out in Channel

definitions.meaning: a candle flame flickers when almost extinguished

explanation.definitionFit: A candle flickers and wavers as it nearly dies; a roadside drain is also called this.

clue.text: Container vehicle not reversible

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: reversible means the word not is turned round

explanation.surface: A lorry's container vehicle cannot be turned round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversible' turns NOT into TON.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardboard box for milk or juice is a kind of receptacle.

clue.text: Vehicle needs parking, so go by foot

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle

explanation.surface: No parking for the car, so walk.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge on a long walk is to hike wearily.

clue.text: Teaching head rather out of date but more to be relied upon

indicators.note: head means the first letter of teaching

parts.note: rustier means more out of practice or out of date

explanation.surface: A headteacher who is somewhat behind the times but more dependable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' gives T from Teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of trusty, meaning more dependable.

clue.text: Former student about to crack up

indicators.note: about means the former student goes round the word to

parts.note: EX means former, as in ex-wife
L is for learner, a student

explanation.surface: An ex-student is about to have a breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the former student round the word to. To crack up someone is to praise them highly, not to break down.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone warmly is to laud them.

clue.text: Mineral withdrawn from atomic agency

indicators.note: withdrawn from means the letters are taken out of the words atomic agency

explanation.surface: A mineral removed from a nuclear agency's stock.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is inside 'atomic agency'.
explanation.definitionFit: A silicate rock that splits into thin sheets.

clue.text: One-time pupil educated in Remove, from the records

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil
literate means educated

explanation.surface: A former pupil educated in a school's Remove form.
explanation.walkthrough: The Remove is a form in some British public schools, which makes 'Remove' look like a classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase or wipe out is to expunge from the records.

clue.text: Snatches bargain, taking a step back

parts.note: a snip is a bargain

indicators.note: back means the step is read backwards

explanation.surface: A shopper grabs a bargain while stepping back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns STEP into PETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Snatches are fragments or scraps, like bits of song.

clue.text: Truly a soldier to join forces

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a soldier
to ally is to join forces

explanation.surface: An honest soldier signs up to unite with others.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuinely or indeed, an adverb of sincerity.
